blocks.text: 1. Hidden State

blocks.alt: An input feeds into the hidden state which produces the output

blocks.text: Vanilla RNN, the previous topic, introduced a concrete network combining input with a previous hidden state. Hidden State gives a closer, more complete look at this module's own central mechanism, explored in complete depth throughout this topic.
It is the genuinely evolving summary a Recurrent Neural Network carries forward across time steps, a genuinely essential concept covered throughout the rest of this topic.

3. What The Hidden State Genuinely Represents

blocks.alt: Past inputs are compressed into the hidden state as a summary

blocks.text: A genuinely important interpretive idea connects back to Feature Maps, already covered in the CNN module. The hidden state genuinely encodes everything the network considers genuinely relevant from the sequence so far.
This is a genuinely direct parallel to feature maps already covered there, just evolving across time instead of representing a fixed spatial pattern within a single image.

blocks.text: 4. A Fixed-Size Summary

blocks.alt: An arbitrarily long history is compressed into a fixed size vector

blocks.text: This connects back to the context vector, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. The hidden state is genuinely a fixed-size vector, regardless of how many time steps have already passed.
This is exactly the same kind of fixed-size compression already covered as the context vector there, just updated continuously at every step rather than computed just once at the very end.
5. Updated At Every Step

blocks.alt: The hidden state updates from t to t+1 to t+2

blocks.text: This connects back to the core idea, already covered in Vanilla RNN. The hidden state genuinely gets updated at every single time step, blending old information with the new current input.
This is a genuinely continuous, ongoing process rather than a one-time computation, the exact update rule already covered in complete detail in the previous topic.
6. The Initial Hidden State

blocks.alt: An initial hidden state of zeros feeds into the first time step

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real practical detail connects back to Weight Initialization, already covered in its own module. The genuinely very first hidden state, before any input has been seen, commonly starts at all zeros.
This mirrors the deliberate choices already covered throughout Weight Initialization, just applied here to the network's own starting memory rather than its learnable weights.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Unlike the learnable weights already covered in Weight Initialization, the initial hidden state, already covered in this topic, is typically not learned itself; it simply provides a genuinely neutral, consistent starting point for every sequence.

blocks.text: 7. The Hidden State As Working Memory

blocks.alt: The hidden state is like working memory

blocks.text: This connects back to the temporal dependency concept, already covered in Sequence Data. The hidden state genuinely functions as the network's own working memory, carrying forward genuinely relevant context across time.
This directly enables the temporal dependencies already covered as sequence data's own defining property, letting the network genuinely connect information across genuinely different time steps.
8. Recapping The Compression Limit

This connects back to the information bottleneck issue, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. A genuinely fixed-size hidden state can only genuinely hold so much information at once, already covered as a real limitation there.

This is the exact same fundamental limitation already covered as that earlier topic's own honest tradeoff, now understood specifically in terms of the hidden state's own fixed-size nature covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why Understanding The Hidden State Genuinely Matters

blocks.alt: Debugging an RNN points toward inspecting the hidden state

blocks.text: This connects back to every Recurrent Neural Network variant covered throughout the rest of this module. Every single one of them genuinely refines how the hidden state gets updated, already covered in this topic.
Debugging why a Sequence Model forgets earlier context is another genuine case where understanding the hidden state's own fixed-size nature, already covered, directly explains why.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates observing how a hidden state evolves and gradually loses fine-grained detail from early time steps, illustrating the compression limit already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 4

def update_hidden_state(h_previous, x_t, decay=0.7):
    # a genuinely simplified stand-in showing how new information genuinely blends with, and gradually overrides, old information
    return np.tanh(decay * h_previous + (1 - decay) * x_t)

hidden_state = np.zeros(hidden_size)
sequence = [rng.normal(size=hidden_size) for _ in range(10)]

first_input_influence = []
for t, x_t in enumerate(sequence):
    hidden_state = update_hidden_state(hidden_state, x_t)
    # measuring how much the very first input still genuinely influences the current hidden state
    influence = np.abs(np.corrcoef(hidden_state, sequence[0])[0, 1])
    first_input_influence.append(influence)
    print(f"Time step {t}: hidden state = {np.round(hidden_state, 3)}, influence of time step 0's input: {influence:.3f}")

print("\nNotice the influence of the very first input genuinely fades over time, already covered as the compression limit in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the measured influence of the very first input gradually fading as more time steps get processed, exactly the fixed-size compression limit already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: The hidden state is the evolving, fixed-size summary a Recurrent Neural Network carries forward.
It encodes everything the network considers genuinely relevant from the sequence so far.
It stays a fixed size regardless of how many time steps have already passed.
It gets updated at every single time step, blending old information with the new current input.
The initial hidden state, before any input is seen, commonly starts at all zeros.
It functions as the network's own working memory, enabling temporal dependencies.
A fixed-size hidden state can only hold so much information, limiting very long sequences.
Every Recurrent Neural Network variant covered later in this module refines how this update happens.
